scope: Both APIs release cached implicit private-IUnknown entries under the existing temporary device self pin, before dropping that pin and before host/device/cache destruction. Drain reentrant cache insertions while only the temporary pin remains. A callback retaining a public device reference defers subsequent stores until its next final Release. Five orders per API cover empty bindings, device-owned implicit bindings, last public surface, retained device, and reentrant private-store insertion. Public-cache data remains intact while an external surface keeps the device alive. The native harness and real XP query actual device AddRef/Release and cooperative state inside all eleven finalizers per API. The observed count of one during finalization is a project safety contract, not a native HAL finalizer oracle. Native empty/owned/last-public/retained/reentrant tests use real device/cache/public/private-data methods; owned binding setup is modeled in C, and XP exercises full SDK setters. No drawing, Clear, Present, Reset, protocol, host, shader or bundle changes. Implicit/additional public binding counts, other resource families, general root-state preservation, arbitrary callback ownership/thread/device-loss graphs, original Microsoft HAL, games/FPS and review stages 4/5/6 remain open.

sources.evidence: Supporting cached surface and public zero/nonzero ownership context only. The protected pending-destruction callback count of one is a bridge safety invariant, not an original Microsoft HAL measurement.
